winner.title: Naengmyeon (Cold Noodles in Chilled Beef Broth)

evidence.authenticity: Eric Kim is a Korean-American authority. Recipe is the beef yuksu plus dongchimi-or-water mul naengmyeon, described as the North Korean cold noodle dish. Short rib broth is chilled, de-fatted and re-simmered with radish, pear, onion and daepa, then slushed. Uses dry naengmyeon noodles, as most home cooks must.
evidence.precision: Only 1 of 22 ingredients has a weight (radish 1 lb), but sizes are specific (3 1/2 lb short ribs, 1 to 2 inches thick; 22 oz noodle package; 2 quarts broth yield). Cues in steps: skim foam, broth rich and meaty, darker and more fragrant, 'assertively seasoned' because served cold, slushied, noodles rinsed until not sticky. Dutch oven or stockpot, no exact pan size.
evidence.testing: NYT Cooking test process. Headnote explains why: the water and freezing to slush make a savory cold broth, why to over-season for cold service, and gives dongchimi vs tap water options. 64 ratings, 4.0 average.
evidence.photos: No step images in schema; page has 46 images but process photos not confirmed (login-hidden content, not marked down heavily).
evidence.efficiency: About 5 hours of simmering plus overnight chill and 1-2 hours freezing. Long but the double-simmer is for flavor. Cucumber and radish pickle in parallel with the noodles.
evidence.access: Korean radish, Korean pear, daepa, yangjo vinegar and maesil cheong all have US subs listed (daikon, Bosc, scallions, distilled white vinegar, maesil optional). Dry naengmyeon is in H Mart and many Asian grocers.

winner.why: Only candidate that makes the full beef-and-radish broth the traditional way with test-kitchen reasoning and specific cues, ahead of Korean Bapsang, which is thinner on explanation and has only 3 weights.

runnerUp.title: Naengmyeon (Cold Noodles)

evidence.authenticity: Korean author. Brisket broth with optional dongchimi, sweet and sour radish, vinegar and hot mustard on the side. Also covers bibim naengmyeon, which is Hamhung style.
evidence.precision: Brisket 230 g, 14 cups water, 5 cups broth for 2; cues: meat tender, broth slushy, cucumber wilted, noodles very cold. Only 3 weights, no pan sizes.
evidence.testing: Established blog with 4.82 rating over 33 ratings. Some reasoning on dongchimi substitution and seasoning.
evidence.photos: 93 images on page, none in schema; photos not confirmed as process shots.
evidence.efficiency: About 1 hour of simmering plus 1-2 hours freezing, quick.
evidence.access: Needs Korean radish, soup soy sauce and Korean pear, with few subs given.

runnerUp.why: Faster and well liked, but less detailed than the NYT recipe on broth building and seasoning.

candidates.disqualified: Not disqualified outright, but it copies Korean Bapsang text, swaps in pheasant, has no process photos and no dongchimi method.

searches: mul naengmyeon buckwheat noodles cold broth recipe
notes: Every English recipe uses dried naengmyeon noodles, which are often part starch. True Pyongyang noodles are mostly buckwheat and hand-pressed, so none is perfectly traditional. Maangchi's main version uses packaged broth and only the variation is traditional. Maangchi and the Food Dictator pages had no structured data, so I read them with WebFetch. NYT page is paywalled in part, so the photos and testing scores are judged from the publisher's process. The Korean 10000recipe results were not read.
